newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Van Ommeren comments on 1996 operations.
newsitem.headline: Van Ommeren comments on 1996 operations.

text.p: Shipping and tank storage firm Koninklijke van Ommeren NV said on Thursday three main business developments had stood out in 1996:
-- a shift of emphasis towards storage and transport of chemicals.
-- increased involvement in shipping and storage of gas.

-- further expansion of worldwide transport and terminal network through addition of 1.5 million cubic metres of storage capacity (of which 55 pct for gas) and acquisition of stake in chemical shipping specialist Iver Ships.
Van Ommeren made the following comments on 1996 operations:

TANK STORAGE -- Development of European market in second half of 1996 was in line with first half but earnings rose as a result of acquisitions. Chemical storage results remained good, though contribution to earnings was lower than in strong 1995. In petroleum storage, long-term contracts helped counter pressure on storage rates. Earnings from storage of vegetable oils remained at satisfactory levels. Contribution to earnings from U.S. declined in second half of year due to lower demand for storage of petroleum products, but fourth quarter showed a recovery. Earnings in Asia stabilised at satisfactory level.

TANKER SHIPPING -- Operating profits for 1996 included book profit of 10 million guilders on sale of ships versus 17.6 million in 1995. Operating results from ocean tanker shipping showed considerable improvement due to gradual strengthening of the dollar, addition of three double-hulled tankers to fleet and contribution from Brostroms/United Tankers. Higher contribution from inland tanker shipping was a result of consolidation of gas tanker shipping company Chemgas and improvement in operational results in second half of the year.

TRANSPORT SERVICES -- Contribution from dry-cargo shipping was lower as result of sale of majority stake in dry bulk unit Van Ommeren Shipping. Operational results of heavy-lift shipping remained at favourable level. Except for agencies, earnings from other operations were higher.
